Name: AgentDeck
Description: Monitor and steer AI coding agents from your D200H or D200X.

Actions.Name: AgentDeck
Actions.Tooltip: AgentDeck — fill your keys with this; each key reflows by agent state (sessions, options, mode, stop, usage). Press to act.

Localization.lede: One key per AI coding session — live state on the key, and your answer sent back.
Localization.s1MacApp: Install AgentDeck Dashboard — free on the Mac App Store, macOS 26 or later — and open it. No terminal needed.
Localization.s1MacOr: On an earlier macOS, or where the App Store app is not offered, use Terminal:
Localization.s1MacNote: The Terminal path needs Node.js 22 or later. It installs the agentdeck command, starts the daemon now and at every login, and installs hooks for the coding agents it finds.
Localization.s1MacDesktop: Codex sessions started in the ChatGPT app show up too, once Codex integration is registered: the Terminal setup does it for you, and the App Store app asks in Settings.
Localization.s1MacTrouble: Keys still OFFLINE? With the app, check that it is running — its icon is in the menu bar. With the Terminal path, run the command again — it is safe to repeat.
Localization.s1Win: Open Windows Terminal, PowerShell or Command Prompt and run:
Localization.s1WinNote: Needs Node.js 22 or later. Setup installs the agentdeck command, starts the daemon now and at every sign-in, and installs hooks for the coding agents it finds.
Localization.s1WinPs: If PowerShell says running scripts is disabled (npx.ps1), run the same line in Command Prompt (cmd.exe), or type npx.cmd in place of npx.
Localization.s1WinTrouble: Keys still OFFLINE? Run the command again — it is safe to repeat — then press Check again. If npx is not found, install Node.js and open a new terminal window.
Localization.s2Body: In any project folder, start your agent the way you normally do — claude, codex or opencode. There is no AgentDeck-specific command.
Localization.s2Hooks: Sessions reach AgentDeck through hooks. The step 1 command installs them for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Kiro — whichever it finds on this computer. Installed an agent after setup? Run the step 1 command again.
Localization.s3Body: Drop the AgentDeck action on every key you want to use — it is the only action there is, and each key decides for itself what to show. The layout spreads over exactly the keys you placed: one per session first, then the answer keys, mode, stop and usage as room allows.
Localization.s3Note: Until step 1 is done, your keys form one dark OFFLINE card. With the daemon running but no agent session yet, they read HUB READY and NO SESSION. Either way the plugin is working — it is showing you which step is missing.
Localization.keysSession: One key per session: the agent, the project, and whether it is working, waiting for you, or done.
Localization.keysDetail: Press a session key to open it. BACK, labelled with the session's name, returns to the list; the next key shows what the session is doing; when the agent asks a question, its answers appear as keys; the last key is Stop, where the session allows it.
Localization.keysUsage: Usage keys show how much of your Claude and Codex subscription limits is used in the current 5-hour and 7-day windows.
Localization.thin: AgentDeck is a thin client, like an OBS plugin: it draws what the local daemon reports and bundles no daemon of its own.
Localization.foundOpaque: Something is answering on port {port} — that is the daemon.
Localization.notFound: No AgentDeck daemon answered on this computer.
Localization.detailNoSession: No agent session yet. Do step 2 and the keys fill in.
Localization.detailHooksMissing: No agent session yet, and Claude Code has no AgentDeck hooks. Install Claude Code if you have not, then run the setup command again.
Localization.detailSession: A session is live. Your keys should be showing it now.
Localization.detailOpaque: This panel cannot read the details from here, so step 2 is unchecked. The keys themselves are the real indicator.
Localization.detailNotFound: Start with step 1. If it is running and this still finds nothing, the check may be blocked here — trust the keys.
Localization.tutorialOpened: Opens in a separate window, which may appear behind the Ulanzi Studio window.
